identity.name: Century Village at Pembroke Pines
identity.hoa_name: Century Village of Pembroke Pines (CVP) Master Association
identity.notes: Master-planned community in Pembroke Pines, Florida, structured as dozens of individual condo associations operating under the CVP master umbrella. Each building is its own legal entity with its own board, budget, insurance, reserve fund, and monthly fee. Owners pay two bills: the CVP recreational fee and their building's condo association fee.

fees.note: CVP master association recreational fee, approximately $238–$276/month in 2026 (varies by unit size and assessment category). Covers clubhouse, pools, security, courtesy bus, cable, internet, and water. Relatively uniform across all units in the community. Example totals: Buckingham building total ~$789/month; Plymouth total ~$623/month (CVP fee + building fee). Building-level condo association fees range roughly $280–$550/month depending on building age, roof condition, reserve fund health, and master insurance premium. Buildings that deferred maintenance may face a one-time special assessment of $15,000–$25,000 per unit for SB 4-D / HB 913 structural reserve compliance. Florida law (SB 4-D / HB 913) requires condo associations to maintain funded reserves for eight structural components. Master property insurance is the largest budget line item: a 100+ unit building may pay $300,000–$500,000 annually (good condition) up to $800,000–$1.5M+ (older roof, claims history), passed through to owners via the monthly fee (e.g., $500K premium ≈ $417/month per unit on a 100-unit building; $1.2M ≈ $1,000/month per unit).

Example building-level condo association fee for the Buckingham buildings (~$513/month), making total monthly obligation ~$789 including the CVP recreational fee. Building fees vary widely across the community (roughly $280–$550/month) based on insurance, reserves, roof condition, and age.

Example building-level condo association fee for Plymouth (~$385/month), making total monthly obligation ~$623 including the CVP recreational fee. The $166/month (~$1,992/year) difference vs. Buckingham is driven by building age, roof condition, reserve fund health, and master insurance premium.

Potential one-time special assessment of $15,000–$25,000 per unit for SB 4-D / HB 913 structural reserve compliance, applicable to buildings that deferred maintenance for a decade. Not a recurring fee; amount is a range and depends on the specific building's reserve fund health.

CVP (master association) recreational fee, approximately $238-$276/month in 2026; difference depends on unit size and specific CVP assessment categories. Every unit owner pays this plus their building's separate condo association fee (two bills total). Fee data per MLS disclosures/listing descriptions as of spring 2026; verify with the specific building association. Covers community-wide amenities (clubhouse, pools, security). Not an official HOA source - blog citing MLS disclosures, so confidence moderate. No CDD assessment found; community is condo-association based, not CDD-based (see open_questions).

Total combined monthly fee (CVP + building condo fee) for a low-fee building; mid-fee building ~$650/month; high-fee building ~$789/month. Building-level fees diverge dramatically by insurance premium, reserve fund health, building age, unit count, and management.
Buckingham building annual HOA (~$789/month) vs ~$5,880/year for a newer-era building - a $3,588/year difference. Fees change annually.
55places lists HOA dues range $174-$701/mo. Conflicts with nova55living's combined totals of ~$530-$789/mo; both versions reported as-is.
